title: Smooth integral envelope of a rational Chevalley root cell
statement:
Let $\mathcal R=(M,\Phi,M^\vee,\Phi^\vee)$ be a finite reduced root datum as in [def-sfb-pinned-split-root-realization], with $\Phi$ spanning $M\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and $\mathbf Z\Phi^\vee=M^\vee$. Let $(G,T=D_{\mathbf Q}(M))$ be a split realization over $\mathbf Q$ of this datum, with no prescribed base or pinning. There exist a base $\Delta$, its positive roots $\Phi^+$, orderings of $\Phi^+$ and $-\Phi^+$, a smooth separated $\mathbf Z$-group scheme $H$ of finite presentation, an immersed torus homomorphism $j:D_{\mathbf Z}(M)\to H$, and immersed homomorphisms $x_\alpha:\mathbf G_{a,\mathbf Z}\to H$ for all $\alpha\in\Phi$. Immersed means identifying the source with a locally closed subscheme. Here $\mathbf G_a(R)=(R,+)$ and $D_R(M)=\operatorname{Spec}R[M]$ has the Hopf operations of [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]; smoothness and finite presentation have the meanings of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and separatedness means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Multiplication gives an open immersion
$$\prod_{\alpha\in-\Phi^+}\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}\times D_{\mathbf Z}(M)\times\prod_{\alpha\in\Phi^+}\mathbf A^1_{\mathbf Z}\longrightarrow H,\quad (a,t,b)\longmapsto\left(\prod x_\alpha(a_\alpha)\right)j(t)\left(\prod x_\alpha(b_\alpha)\right),$$
whose image is dense in every geometric fibre. Write $\chi_\alpha(t)=t(e^\alpha)$ and write $j\alpha^\vee$ for the monomial cocharacter $t\mapsto j(D(\alpha^\vee)(t))$. On points over every commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebra one has
$$j(t)x_\alpha(z)j(t)^{-1}=x_\alpha(\chi_\alpha(t)z),$$
and, whenever $1+uv$ is a unit,
$$x_\alpha(u)x_{-\alpha}(v)=x_{-\alpha}\left(\frac v{1+uv}\right)j\alpha^\vee(1+uv)x_\alpha\left(\frac u{1+uv}\right).$$
For $n_\alpha=x_\alpha(1)x_{-\alpha}(-1)x_\alpha(1)$ one has $n_\alpha x_\alpha(z)n_\alpha^{-1}=x_{-\alpha}(-z)$. There is a $\mathbf Q$-group isomorphism $H_{\mathbf Q}\simeq G$ restricting on the displayed torus to the identity and carrying each $x_{\alpha,\mathbf Q}$ to a parametrization of the root subgroup labelled $\alpha$. Neither affineness of $H$ nor reductivity of its special fibres is assumed or asserted here. The zero datum is allowed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-birational-law] to the given rational realization. It supplies the base, orders, parameters, explicit smooth integral cell $C$, and a strict integral partial multiplication agreeing with $G$ over $\mathbf Q$. All lattice hypotheses are exactly those assumed here; no pinning is prescribed. The fibre rings of $C$ are polynomial Laurent polynomial rings, including the rank-zero case.

Apply [lem-sfb-dedekind-strict-law-realization] with $R=\mathbf Z$ and $X=C$ to obtain $i:C\hookrightarrow H$. The Euclidean algorithm makes every ideal of $\mathbf Z$ principal, so $\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian; in $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ every nonzero ideal is $(p^r)$, and the unique maximal ideal is the nonzero $(p)$, verifying the DVR hypothesis. The preceding node supplies smoothness, separatedness, finite presentation, nonempty fibres and precisely the required strictness. Thus $H$ is smooth separated and finitely presented, and $i(C)$ is dense in every fibre. By [lem-sfb-smooth-fibrewise-dense-open-base-change] applied to the smooth $H$ and its open chart, this remains dense after any base change, in particular on every geometric fibre. Let $j=i q_T$ and $x_\alpha=i q_\alpha$. Each coordinate map identifies an explicit closed coordinate subscheme of $C$, so its composite with the open chart is an immersion.

The two group schemes $H_{\mathbf Q}$ and $G$ contain the same dense open $C_{\mathbf Q}$, and its multiplications agree as rational maps. By [lem-sfb-rational-group-hom-extension], $c\circ i_{\mathbf Q}^{-1}$ extends uniquely to a group isomorphism $H_{\mathbf Q}\simeq G$. On the coordinate axes and torus it has the prescribed restrictions. Its restriction to the torus is the identity under the given $D_{\mathbf Q}(M)$ identifications.

All required remaining claims are equalities of morphisms into the separated $H$ and hold over $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-sfb-chevalley-integral-birational-law] and the preceding isomorphism. For the homomorphism assertions the domains are $\mathbf A^2_{\mathbf Z}$ and $T\times T$; for the product-chart equality the domain is $C$; for torus conjugation it is $T\times\mathbf A^1$; for the opposite-root formula it is $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[u,v,(1+uv)^{-1}]$; and for Weyl conjugation it is $\mathbf A^1$. Each coordinate ring is a polynomial Laurent polynomial ring or its indicated localization, hence injects into its tensor product with $\mathbf Q$. The generic fibre is therefore scheme-theoretically dominant in each domain. Apply [lemma-nagata-ext-scheme-theoretically-dominant-separated] to conclude these equalities over $\mathbf Z$. In particular the ordered product map is exactly $i$, so is the required open immersion. Equality of these morphisms gives the identities on points over every commutative $\mathbf Z$-algebra, including nonreduced ones. The construction also applies when the root datum is zero, with $C=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

Strictness makes the two translation maps S-birational, because D is dense in every fibre of the open projection. Step 3: I checked every hypothesis of lem-sfb-rational-group-hom-extension over Q, including a(i(x)i(y)) = c(m(x,y)) = c(x)c(y) on a dense open. Step 4: the Nagata equality lemma holds for any scheme-theoretically dominant map. Each domain ring (Z[u,v], Z[M+M], O(C), Z[M][z], Z[u,v,(1+uv)^-1], Z[z]) is torsion-free, so its generic fibre is dominant, and the target H is separated. This is Conrad's 'check over Q'. Small cases checked in SL2: the rank-one formula for both alpha and -alpha, the Weyl relation for both, u=0 or v=0, and no characteristic constant is inverted. The Dedekind node is true: spread the generic solution over a dense open, handle the finitely many remaining closed points by the DVR solutions, and glue using uniqueness. It strictly generalizes the existing field/DVR node, which cannot be applied with R=Z.
